A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Value Profiles for Encoding Human Variation. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated sections and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across six datasets, including representation comparisons, clustering, interpretability, calibration, and population simulation, with additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and supplies corrected and additional qualitative cluster outputs in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The prompted value encoder, supervised decoder training, predictive-information estimation, and clustering procedure remain unchanged. Appendix H revises reported cluster outputs without establishing a change to the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpinionQA, Hatespeech-Kumar, DICES, ValuePrism, Habermas-Likert, and PRISM. Habermas free-form justification prediction and cross-dataset zero-shot evaluation already appear in v1 Appendix C; the expanded cluster listings introduce no new coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator settings remain in Tables 4–9 and Appendix C. The Habermas party baseline disappears from the main clustering plot, but its corresponding result remains in Table 8, indicating a display omission rather than removal from the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix A corrects the stated evaluation-set size to total ratings minus fit-set ratings; v1 Section 11 mistakenly subtracts evaluation-set ratings. This corrects the reported partition specification without establishing that experiments were rerun. Other splits, models, budgets, metrics, and sampling procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The qualitative evidence about cluster disagreement modes is substantially revised. Appendix H replaces repeated DICES descriptions under other dataset headings with dataset-specific profiles and adds PRISM four/eight-cluster and ValuePrism two/four/eight-cluster cases. The other supplementary analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 removes significance stars from the representation-performance plots and deletes v1 Figure 4's explanation of mixed-linear-effects testing against the no-information condition. Five random splits and the existing confidence-interval reporting remain; no increase in repeated runs is reported.

E6.justification: Appendix H substantially corrects and expands qualitative results: Habermas, Hatespeech-Kumar, OpinionQA, and PRISM receive distinct cluster descriptions instead of repeated DICES outputs, and previously missing cluster descriptions are supplied. Tables 2 and 4–9, information-preservation percentages, and calibration and zero-shot scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The partition equation is corrected from |D_eval_i| = |D_i| - |D_eval_i| to |D_eval_i| = |D_i| - |D_fit_i|. This is a limited mathematical correction; the V-information definitions, clustering formulation, and Appendix D uncertainty decomposition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: natural-language value profiles preserve over 70% of usable demonstration information, support predictive clustering, and enable interpretable, calibrated individual modeling. The revised appendix supplies evidence for existing claims.

C2.justification: v2's ethical discussion removes the specific warning that performance may degrade for values poorly understood or represented in natural language. The model-family limitation is retained after relocation, and Appendix D preserves the uncertainty interpretation shortened in the main text.

D1.justification: The fit/eval partition documentation is corrected, while Algorithm 2 loses its explanation that the NV × NX decoder calls dominate runtime. Decoder hyperparameters, precision handling, prompts, preprocessing instructions, and hardware information are otherwise retained, including material moved to Appendix A.

R1.justification: Section 8 adds Hu and Collier's demographic-persona findings and Poddar et al.'s variational preference learning, distinguishing its vector-valued latent representation from natural-language profiles. The Lippert-Rasmussen citation is removed. Most other reference changes concern formatting or shortened author lists.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected passages are tightened, limitations move into the main text, and reproducibility details move to Appendix A. Most prose and the research narrative remain intact. Some editing defects are introduced, including duplicated wording in Sections 5 and 7.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with resized and repositioned figures, tables, algorithms, and profile listings. The illustrative V-information plot moves to the appendix, plot labels and axes are revised, and the Habermas party comparator is omitted from the clustering plot.

improvement.justification: Correcting the dataset-mismatched profiles and completing Appendix H makes the qualitative evidence supporting Section 6 substantially more credible and inspectable. The partition correction and related-work additions also help. These reporting improvements outweigh the losses, but removal of significance-test documentation and a specific limitation, alongside new editing errors, limits the overall gain.
